"definitions": [
{"id": "d1", "term": "relevance", "verbatim_text": "In order to have relevance, statistics must meet the needs of users.", "normative_status": "academic", "as_of_date": null, "anchor": "In order to have relevance", "location": "Appendix 1"},
{"id": "d2", "term": "Relevance", "verbatim_text": "Relevance is the degree to which statistics meet current and potential user needs.", "normative_status": "standard", "as_of_date": null, "anchor": "Relevance is the degree", "location": "Appendix 1"},
{"id": "d3", "term": "Accuracy", "verbatim_text": "Accuracy in the general statistical sense denotes the closeness of computations or estimates to the (unknown) exact or true values.", "normative_status": "standard", "as_of_date": null, "anchor": "Accuracy in the general statistical", "location": "Appendix 1"},
{"id": "d4", "term": "Timeliness", "verbatim_text": "Timeliness of information reflects the length of time between its availability and the event or phenomenon it describes.", "normative_status": "standard", "as_of_date": null, "anchor": "Timeliness of information reflects", "location": "Appendix 1"},
{"id": "d5", "term": "Punctuality", "verbatim_text": "Punctuality refers to the time lag between the release date of data and the target date when it should have been delivered", "normative_status": "standard", "as_of_date": null, "anchor": "Punctuality refers to the time lag", "location": "Appendix 1"},
{"id": "d6", "term": "Accessibility", "verbatim_text": "Accessibility refers to the physical conditions under which users can obtain data", "normative_status": "standard", "as_of_date": null, "anchor": "Accessibility refers to the physical", "location": "Appendix 1"},
{"id": "d7", "term": "Clarity", "verbatim_text": "Clarity refers to the data’s information environment whether data are accompanied with appropriate documentation and metadata", "normative_status": "standard", "as_of_date": null, "anchor": "Clarity refers to the", "location": "Appendix 1"},
{"id": "d8", "term": "Coherence", "verbatim_text": "Coherence of statistics is their adequacy to be reliably combined in different ways and for various uses.", "normative_status": "standard", "as_of_date": null, "anchor": "Coherence of statistics is their", "location": "Appendix 1"},
{"id": "d9", "term": "Comparability", "verbatim_text": "Comparability aims at measuring the impact of differences in applied statistical concepts and measurement tools/procedures", "normative_status": "standard", "as_of_date": null, "anchor": "Comparability aims at measuring", "location": "Appendix 1"}
],

"claims": [
{"id": "k1", "claim_text": "The challenges of collecting and integrating data can be met.", "claim_type": "empirical", "evidence_grade": "inference", "anchor": "challenges of collecting and integrating data", "location": "8. Conclusions"},
{"id": "k2", "claim_text": "In terms of data quality, as opposed to documentation, the Transparent Reporting Project found that user evaluations are high for relevance, accuracy, reliability and coherence.", "claim_type": "empirical", "evidence_grade": "measured_practitioner", "anchor": "user evaluations are high for relevance", "location": "8. Conclusions"},
{"id": "k3", "claim_text": "Users are also confident in the data and statistics.", "claim_type": "empirical", "evidence_grade": "measured_practitioner", "anchor": "confident in the data and statistics", "location": "8. Conclusions"},
{"id": "k4", "claim_text": "Users were less satisfied with data quality in terms of comparability, access, timeliness, and punctuality.", "claim_type": "empirical", "evidence_grade": "measured_practitioner", "anchor": "Users were less satisfied", "location": "8. Conclusions"},
{"id": "k5", "claim_text": "Like the challenges of data quality, the challenges of transparent reporting can be met.", "claim_type": "empirical", "evidence_grade": "inference", "anchor": "challenges of transparent reporting can be met", "location": "8. Conclusions"},
{"id": "k6", "claim_text": "Importantly, the Transparent Reporting Project found that agency staff are a valued source of information for users.", "claim_type": "empirical", "evidence_grade": "measured_practitioner", "anchor": "agency staff are a valued source", "location": "8. Conclusions"},
{"id": "k7", "claim_text": "Other clusters of items that with relatively high percentages of positive ratings were general-level quality of documentation and agency evaluation of quality.", "claim_type": "empirical", "evidence_grade": "measured_practitioner", "anchor": "relatively high percentages of positive ratings", "location": "8. Conclusions"},
{"id": "k8", "claim_text": "There is room for agencies to improve on the transparency—that is, the clarity and completeness —of their documentation, by providing more detail on source data, data integration, and how to use the statistical product.", "claim_type": "normative", "evidence_grade": "inference", "anchor": "There is room for agencies to improve", "location": "8. Conclusions"},
{"id": "k9", "claim_text": "All in all, results from the Transparent Reporting Project suggest that, however agencies do it, the agencies in the project are meeting many of the documentation needs of their users with current reporting approaches.", "claim_type": "empirical", "evidence_grade": "inference", "anchor": "meeting many of the documentation needs", "location": "8. Conclusions"},
{"id": "k10", "claim_text": "The format of documentation ranges from a report dedicated exclusively to the product, to targeted webpages, to a compendium of sources and methods.", "claim_type": "empirical", "evidence_grade": "measured_practitioner", "anchor": "to a compendium of sources", "location": "8. Conclusions"},
{"id": "k11", "claim_text": "Statistics should accurately and reliably portray reality.", "claim_type": "normative", "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion", "anchor": "accurately and reliably portray reality", "location": "Appendix 1"},
{"id": "k12", "claim_text": "Statistics should be released in a timely and punctual manner.", "claim_type": "normative", "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion", "anchor": "timely and punctual manner", "location": "Appendix 1"},
{"id": "k13", "claim_text": "Eurostat recommends that agencies ensure that they follow proper release dates and times and make sure to publish the time that outputs will be published.", "claim_type": "normative", "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion", "anchor": "Eurostat recommends that agencies", "location": "Appendix 1"},
{"id": "k14", "claim_text": "Statistics should be presented in a clear and understandable form, released in a suitable and convenient manner, and available and accessible on an impartial basis with supporting metadata and guidance.", "claim_type": "normative", "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion", "anchor": "clear and understandable form", "location": "Appendix 1"},
{"id": "k15", "claim_text": "Statistics should be consistent internally and over time and comparable among regions and countries.", "claim_type": "normative", "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion", "anchor": "consistent internally and over time", "location": "Appendix 1"},
{"id": "k16", "claim_text": "A basic distinction is between sampling and non-sampling errors, which are both subject to variability as well as bias.", "claim_type": "empirical", "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion", "anchor": "A basic distinction is between", "location": "Appendix 1"}
